Consider the partition of the rectangular region $R$ shown above and the positive function $f(x,y)$ defined on $R.$ Which of the following gives an expression for the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to this partition.

*Hint: ${M}_{ij}$ denotes the maximum value of $f$ on the subregion ${R}_{ij}$*" :question/worked-solution "To calculate the upper Riemann sum $U$ with respect to the given partition, we compute the sum of the volumes of $3$ rectangular solids, one for each ${R}_{ij}.$

The volume of the rectangular solid corresponding to each subregion ${R}_{ij}$ is given by

$$
{M}_{ij}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{ij}).
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ denotes the maximum value of $f$ on the subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

So in our case, we have

$$
U={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{M}_{13}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{13}).
$$

Notice that

$$
\text{Area}({R}_{11})=\text{Area}({R}_{12})=\text{Area}({R}_{13})=2.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =2\cdot {M}_{11}+2\cdot {M}_{12}+2\cdot {M}_{13} \\  & =2({M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186148895 :answer-field/correct "answer-5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" :answer-field/choices ["answer-5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" "answer-d79c99a8-657e-5f1b-9bf1-7b78ca1c5271" "answer-e0699502-562e-5567-92d0-a0fdd69f0682" "answer-d9dffb21-59c0-5a1f-8919-0d8e4cb108a1" "answer-548eea5d-4b28-5e16-b164-434012c34f08"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" :answer/id #uuid "5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2({M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d79c99a8-657e-5f1b-9bf1-7b78ca1c5271" :answer/id #uuid "d79c99a8-657e-5f1b-9bf1-7b78ca1c5271" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}+2{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e0699502-562e-5567-92d0-a0fdd69f0682" :answer/id #uuid "e0699502-562e-5567-92d0-a0fdd69f0682" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d9dffb21-59c0-5a1f-8919-0d8e4cb108a1" :answer/id #uuid "d9dffb21-59c0-5a1f-8919-0d8e4cb108a1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}-{M}_{12}-{M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-548eea5d-4b28-5e16-b164-434012c34f08" :answer/id #uuid "548eea5d-4b28-5e16-b164-434012c34f08" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}\cdot {M}_{12}\cdot {M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-b7b6e192-3a06-52fc-8d5f-7a6810288b2c" :question/id #uuid "b7b6e192-3a06-52fc-8d5f-7a6810288b2c" :question/math-academy-id "q-123058" :question/problem "![](images/dd/dd73cb7785de514503cba6a04931a88084172b58826efdf22ea847f256c375fb.png)

"Let $R=[-3,-1]\times [1,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=10-4x-2y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{-3,-2,-1\},\,{P}_{2}=\{1,2,3\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$" :question/worked-solution "First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](images/10/10eca85fc2ab60ea0b1ee229b0a0e20110f88c4724088c0f0630d22150a8a08d.png)

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{M}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{M}_{22}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{22}),
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=1$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}+{M}_{21}+{M}_{31}+{M}_{41}.
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=10-4x-2y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=10-4x-2y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](images/ea/eaa3ed265eac5a53eedc07f07e2ff386505a6ea5cc4934653d587e84238b540d.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion.

![](images/c3/c332690fba1843ee09bd1466f1c978c41aff8438bf9b2a23a847ca58e2f9c228.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{11} & =f(-3,1)=20 \\ {M}_{21} & =f(-2,1)=16 \\ {M}_{12} & =f(-3,2)=18 \\ {M}_{22} & =f(-2,2)=14\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =20+16+18+14 \\  & =68.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-1d634307-c7b5-59ff-9b60-846917abd3ed"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-1d634307-c7b5-59ff-9b60-846917abd3ed" :answer-field/id #uuid "1d634307-c7b5-59ff-9b60-846917abd3ed" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-50aeb266-ab0d-5212-9160-89d504220b88" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8d1a5a83-6b20-57f5-b4fb-8472a5b67928" "answer-7b106611-ae0e-5111-91d1-a39c2610f56d" "answer-342a7334-6ebf-59b7-8331-37af5e6b4d2c" "answer-de92d4f3-fc6c-5524-b29c-1a39a0e93889" "answer-50aeb266-ab0d-5212-9160-89d504220b88"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8d1a5a83-6b20-57f5-b4fb-8472a5b67928" :answer/id #uuid "8d1a5a83-6b20-57f5-b4fb-8472a5b67928" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "36" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7b106611-ae0e-5111-91d1-a39c2610f56d" :answer/id #uuid "7b106611-ae0e-5111-91d1-a39c2610f56d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "48" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-342a7334-6ebf-59b7-8331-37af5e6b4d2c" :answer/id #uuid "342a7334-6ebf-59b7-8331-37af5e6b4d2c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "50" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-de92d4f3-fc6c-5524-b29c-1a39a0e93889" :answer/id #uuid "de92d4f3-fc6c-5524-b29c-1a39a0e93889" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "60" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-50aeb266-ab0d-5212-9160-89d504220b88" :answer/id #uuid "50aeb266-ab0d-5212-9160-89d504220b88" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "68" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-e0e69171-a8d5-534f-acb8-6c56c972aa07" :question/id #uuid "e0e69171-a8d5-534f-acb8-6c56c972aa07" :question/math-academy-id "q-123243" :question/problem "Let $R=[0,5]\times [1,5]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=100-{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{0,5\},\,{P}_{2}=\{1,3,5\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$" :question/worked-solution "First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](images/77/77fdf238fb2b4046da6ddc69024378a56e4de5f46de301d5fac094cbc290b23b.png)

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12}),
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=10$ for both subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =10\cdot {M}_{11}+10\cdot {M}_{12} \\  & =10({M}_{11}+{M}_{12}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=100-{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=100-{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](images/62/62871cd2fcc4993e0775fb7bdf0609d7849a1aa2ea5a314bc727967df590d6e7.png)

y>-3

$-4x+5<-7$ is $x${{field-1}}{{field-2}}." :question/worked-solution "First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $5$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x+5 & <-7 \\ -4x+5-5 & <-7-5 \\ -4x+0 & <-12 \\ -4x & <-12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-4.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+10 & \ge 4 \\ -2x+10-10 & \ge 4-10 \\ -2x+0 & \ge -6 \\ -2x & \ge -6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x\,\, & \ge \,\,-6 \\ \frac{-2x}{-2}\, & \le \,\,\frac{-6}{-2} \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}x}{\cancel{-2}}\, & \le \,\,3 \\ x\,\, & \le \,3\end{aligned}
$$

:question/worked-solution "From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1 & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ (z+1)^{2} & =3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1) \\ (z+1) & =\pm \sqrt{3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1 & \ge 0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}=1$, including its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 1\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186323405 :answer-field/correct "answer-8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8a23aa13-d540-5d99-be2b-3b822200ad45" "answer-8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" "answer-6d07251a-4f5b-5fe1-a5c8-5c5e4e7f9bfc" "answer-9bc62f3e-4d97-58eb-bb7f-08bb44e41d57"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8a23aa13-d540-5d99-be2b-3b822200ad45" :answer/id #uuid "8a23aa13-d540-5d99-be2b-3b822200ad45" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}<1\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" :answer/id #uuid "8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 1\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6d07251a-4f5b-5fe1-a5c8-5c5e4e7f9bfc" :answer/id #uuid "6d07251a-4f5b-5fe1-a5c8-5c5e4e7f9bfc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}<0\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9bc62f3e-4d97-58eb-bb7f-08bb44e41d57" :answer/id #uuid "9bc62f3e-4d97-58eb-bb7f-08bb44e41d57" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 0\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-1a64d7fd-d80f-53bd-910a-60419647eb47" :question/id #uuid "1a64d7fd-d80f-53bd-910a-60419647eb47" :question/math-academy-id "q-36323" :question/problem "What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the hyperboloid of one sheet $9{x}^{2}+8{y}^{2}-4{z}^{2}=1?$" :question/worked-solution "To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperboloid. :question/id #uuid "3c0d5e56-2169-54d3-9966-1a109d2d5523" :question/math-academy-id "q-105796" :question/problem "Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(0,-1,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,i+3z\,j-2y\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=(6z-1)\,j.
$$" :question/worked-solution "If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & 3z & -2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(3z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)]k \\  & =(-2-3)i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-5\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-5\,i+(6z-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,-1,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(0,-1,1) & =-5\,i+(6(1)-1)\,j \\  & =-5\,i+5\,j.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-743b8050-afb0-5239-be1f-b571663c2f9a"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-743b8050-afb0-5239-be1f-b571663c2f9a" :answer-field/id #uuid "743b8050-afb0-5239-be1f-b571663c2f9a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" :answer-field/choices ["answer-65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" "answer-504fe88b-8989-50fd-9bf6-4fb3a0874f14" "answer-de460cf2-dd72-57b6-89cf-2648f5feed59" "answer-953d0060-629d-5930-8b1a-dc079696c8e2" "answer-cb311272-e389-523f-83ba-df596e274f53"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" :answer/id #uuid "65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-5\,i+5\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-504fe88b-8989-50fd-9bf6-4fb3a0874f14" :answer/id #uuid "504fe88b-8989-50fd-9bf6-4fb3a0874f14" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-j+k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-de460cf2-dd72-57b6-89cf-2648f5feed59" :answer/id #uuid "de460cf2-dd72-57b6-89cf-2648f5feed59" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-953d0060-629d-5930-8b1a-dc079696c8e2" :answer/id #uuid "953d0060-629d-5930-8b1a-dc079696c8e2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cb311272-e389-523f-83ba-df596e274f53" :answer/id #uuid "cb311272-e389-523f-83ba-df596e274f53" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5\,i-j+5\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186180186 :question/problem "Calculate $∇\times (F+2G)$ at the point $(1,1,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z\,i+{x}^{2}y\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z\,i+(xy-2xyz)\,j-xz\,k.
$$" :question/worked-solution "If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+2G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (2G) \\  & =∇\times F+2∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {x}^{2}z & 0 & {x}^{2}y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}z)]k \\  & =({x}^{2}-0)i-(2xy-{x}^{2})j+(0-0)k \\  & ={x}^{2}\,i+({x}^{2}-2xy)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+2G) & =∇\times F+2∇\times G \\  & ={x}^{2}\,i+({x}^{2}-2xy)\,j+2[{x}^{2}z\,i+(xy-2xyz)\,j-xz\,k] \\  & =({x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}z)\,i+({x}^{2}-2xy+2xy-4xyz)\,j-2xz\,k \\  & ={x}^{2}(1+2z)\,i+({x}^{2}-4xyz)\,j-2xz\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,1,1),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (F+2G))(1,1,1)=3\,i-3\,j-2\,k.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186178660 :answer-field/correct "answer-ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" :answer-field/choices ["answer-0f9b5739-0938-5c65-94b0-f1b4aa69e157" "answer-6a99f0f4-e5ef-5f99-af5c-c942163885d5" "answer-ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" "answer-1067630d-4e4d-554b-9f81-a5561e8e478a" "answer-045f588e-73be-514d-9fd9-46ece75a5e69"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0f9b5739-0938-5c65-94b0-f1b4aa69e157" :answer/id #uuid "0f9b5739-0938-5c65-94b0-f1b4aa69e157" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\,i-3\,j-2\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6a99f0f4-e5ef-5f99-af5c-c942163885d5" :answer/id #uuid "6a99f0f4-e5ef-5f99-af5c-c942163885d5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\,i-\,j+k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" :answer/id #uuid "ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\,i-3\,j-2\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1067630d-4e4d-554b-9f81-a5561e8e478a" :answer/id #uuid "1067630d-4e4d-554b-9f81-a5561e8e478a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\,i-4\,j-4\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-045f588e-73be-514d-9fd9-46ece75a5e69" :answer/id #uuid "045f588e-73be-514d-9fd9-46ece75a5e69" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5\,i-2\,j+k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-0ea54cb1-a0d4-5539-a164-15702dc537d3" :question/id #uuid "0ea54cb1-a0d4-5539-a164-15702dc537d3" :question/math-academy-id "q-105795" :question/problem "Calculate $∇\times (F-3G)$ at the point $(1,0,9)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=(2\sqrt{z}+x)\,i+xy\,j+{y}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=3{x}^{2}y\,k.
$$" :question/worked-solution "If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-3G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (-3G) \\  & =∇\times F-3∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 2\sqrt{z}+x & xy & {y}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\sqrt{z}+x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{z}+x)]k \\  & =(2y-0)i-(0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}})j+(y-0)k \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-3G) & =∇\times F-3∇\times G \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k-3[3{x}^{2}y\,k] \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k-9{x}^{2}y\,k \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y(1-9{x}^{2})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,0,9),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-3G))(1,0,9) & =2(0)\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{9}}\,j+0(1-9(1)^{2})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-523554aa-2a52-5d37-8cc9-84d837bdff76"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-523554aa-2a52-5d37-8cc9-84d837bdff76" :answer-field/id #uuid "523554aa-2a52-5d37-8cc9-84d837bdff76" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a6aa9a17-9981-5e03-a5c9-1692e6dae401" "answer-8f4111c9-6604-575a-b3bf-8b514228499e" "answer-a4873e67-7fec-50d7-b791-b5ed499f85ae" "answer-3c1f5b71-a8d9-5bee-8b46-73f0baef7978" "answer-1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a6aa9a17-9981-5e03-a5c9-1692e6dae401" :answer/id #uuid "a6aa9a17-9981-5e03-a5c9-1692e6dae401" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-9\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8f4111c9-6604-575a-b3bf-8b514228499e" :answer/id #uuid "8f4111c9-6604-575a-b3bf-8b514228499e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-i-\frac{1}{3}\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a4873e67-7fec-50d7-b791-b5ed499f85ae" :answer/id #uuid "a4873e67-7fec-50d7-b791-b5ed499f85ae" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\,i" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3c1f5b71-a8d9-5bee-8b46-73f0baef7978" :answer/id #uuid "3c1f5b71-a8d9-5bee-8b46-73f0baef7978" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "9\,i-3\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2" :answer/id #uuid "1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-1adbaf5f-6695-5acc-8c83-a7d990c62422" :question/id #uuid "1adbaf5f-6695-5acc-8c83-a7d990c62422" :question/math-academy-id "q-105964" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨3z,2x,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xz+y.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,3,2⟩,\,∇f=⟨z,1,x⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,0,0).$" :question/worked-solution "We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ z & 1 & x \\ 3z & 2x & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1(0)-x(2x)]i-[z(0)-x(3z)]j+[z(2x)-1(3z)]k \\  & =-2{x}^{2}\,i+3xz\,j+(2xz-3z)\,k \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(xz+y)⟨0,3,2⟩+⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3(xz+y),2(xz+y)⟩+⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},3(xz+y)+3xz,2(xz+y)+2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},6xz+3y,4xz+2y-3z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,0,0) & =⟨-2(1)^{2},6(1)(0)+3(0),4(1)(0)+2(0)-3(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-358ba299-db97-5c30-b480-8ad69e4c1d58"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-358ba299-db97-5c30-b480-8ad69e4c1d58" :answer-field/id #uuid "358ba299-db97-5c30-b480-8ad69e4c1d58" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" :answer-field/choices ["answer-716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" "answer-9b8592fa-9388-57e4-a3b0-75e82fd0fa0b" "answer-b34859f7-1d1a-5aa1-a406-403532f54aee" "answer-0c8eee1c-f133-5076-90a3-abd6303c7686" "answer-3bc83cd3-ee31-5732-a9e3-7f6452fee0f6"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" :answer/id #uuid "716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨-2,0,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9b8592fa-9388-57e4-a3b0-75e82fd0fa0b" :answer/id #uuid "9b8592fa-9388-57e4-a3b0-75e82fd0fa0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,-2,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b34859f7-1d1a-5aa1-a406-403532f54aee" :answer/id #uuid "b34859f7-1d1a-5aa1-a406-403532f54aee" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,0,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0c8eee1c-f133-5076-90a3-abd6303c7686" :answer/id #uuid "0c8eee1c-f133-5076-90a3-abd6303c7686" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,3,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3bc83cd3-ee31-5732-a9e3-7f6452fee0f6" :answer/id #uuid "3bc83cd3-ee31-5732-a9e3-7f6452fee0f6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨1,-1,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-38f95650-79fd-557c-9c72-45e47bd9ea35" :question/id #uuid "38f95650-79fd-557c-9c72-45e47bd9ea35" :question/math-academy-id "q-131475" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},yz,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{-y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-y,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨{e}^{-y},-x{e}^{-y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,1,2).$" :question/worked-solution "We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {e}^{-y} & -x{e}^{-y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & yz & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(-x{e}^{-y})(0)-(yz)(0)]i-[({e}^{-y})(0)-(x{e}^{y})(0)]j+[({e}^{-y})(yz)-(x{e}^{y})(-x{e}^{-y})]k \\  & =0\,i+0j+(yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2})k \\  & =⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x{e}^{-y})⟨-y,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-xy{e}^{-y},0,-{x}^{2}⟩+⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-xy{e}^{-y},0,yz{e}^{-y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
∇\times (f\,F)(0,1,2)=⟨0,0,\frac{2}{e}⟩.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7200c5c6-834c-582d-bb4f-488640d68497"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(B)$ for every matrix $B?$

I. $\text{Null}({B}^{T})$

II. $\text{Col}(B)$

III. $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$" :question/worked-solution "Recall that $\text{Null}(B)$ contains all vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $B,$ result in the zero-vector $0.$ 

When pre-multiplying a vector by $B,$ we actually multiply each row of $B$ by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(B)$ must be orthogonal to the row space of $B,$ which is $\text{Col}({A}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

It's possible to determine information regarding the multiplicities of the roots of a polynomial from its graph.

- If the graph intersects the $x$-axis but is *not* tangent to the $x$-axis at $x=a,$ we have a *simple* root $x=a.$

- If the graph is *tangent* to the $x$-axis at $x=a,$ we have a *multiple* root $x=a.$ Furthermore:

- If the graph touches the $x$-axis and reverses direction at $x=a,$ the multiplicity of a root $x=a$ is *even*.

- If the graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=a,$ the multiplicity of a root $x=a$ is *odd*.

In our case, the graph is *not* tangent to the $x$-axis at $x=-7.$ Therefore, $x=-7$ is a *simple* root." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields :question/id #uuid "83c46e33-f8bd-5862-a614-a54a16643b82" :question/math-academy-id "q-220358" :question/problem "The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(2x+k)(x-3k)$ is $x=\frac{1}{4}.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=$

{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{4},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{1}{4}.$ 

From the equation $y=(2x+k)(x-3k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{k}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=3k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{k}{2}+3k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6k-k}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{5k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{4}.$ Therefore, we have

{{field-1}}

{{field-3}}
$).$" :question/worked-solution "The critical points of a multivariable function $f$ are the points $a$ in the domain of $f$ such that ${f}^{′}(a)={0}^{T}$ or ${f}^{′}(a)$ does not exist, where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}.
$$

In this case, the domain of $f$ is ${R}^{2},$ and the first derivative of $f$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}8{x}^{3}+16x{y}^{2}-16x & \,16{x}^{2}y+12y\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the critical points, we need to find the points $(x,y)\in {R}^{2}$ such that ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T}$ or ${f}^{′}(x,y)$ does not exist. Note that, in our case, ${f}^{′}(x,y)$ exists everywhere, so we just need to find the points where ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T}.$

Setting ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T},$ we have the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}8{x}^{3}+16x{y}^{2}-16x=0 \\ 16{x}^{2}y+12y=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}8x({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-2)=0 \\ 4y(4{x}^{2}+3)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $4{x}^{2}+3\ne 0,$ from the second equation of the system, we obtain that

$$
y=0.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}8x({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-2) & =0 \\ 8x({x}^{2}+{0}^{2}-2) & =0 \\ 8x({x}^{2}-2) & =0 \\ x & =0,\pm \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the critical points $(\pm \sqrt{2},0)$ and $(0,0).$

Note that since ${f}^{′}(x)={0}^{T}$ at these points, they are also stationary points." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields {{field-2}}" :question/worked-solution "We computed the second partial derivatives in part 5. So, the second derivative of $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}24{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-16 & 32xy \\ 32xy & 16{x}^{2}+12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

* Evaluating the second derivative at $(\pm \sqrt{2},0),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(\pm \sqrt{2},0)=[\begin{aligned}32 & 0 \\ 0 & 44\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we have

$$
H(\pm \sqrt{2},0)=32\cdot 44-0\cdot 0=1\,408.
$$

* Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,0),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,0)=[\begin{aligned}-16 & 0 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we have

$$
H(0,0)=-16\cdot 12-0\cdot 0=-192.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-02a238bb-fadd-5461-8325-d873d6a724ae" "answer-field-0189ae91-6ed6-5d12-a32f-c03fa82da30e"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-02a238bb-fadd-5461-8325-d873d6a724ae" :answer-field/id #uuid "02a238bb-fadd-5461-8325-d873d6a724ae" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-b7d19913-62b2-5223-b8ec-7ca4b1fb9c97" :answer-field/choices ["answer-b7d19913-62b2-5223-b8ec-7ca4b1fb9c97"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b7d19913-62b2-5223-b8ec-7ca4b1fb9c97" :answer/id #uuid "b7d19913-62b2-5223-b8ec-7ca4b1fb9c97" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1408" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-0189ae91-6ed6-5d12-a32f-c03fa82da30e" :answer-field/id #uuid "0189ae91-6ed6-5d12-a32f-c03fa82da30e" :answer-field/key "field-2" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-2d6a5a41-e723-5f75-9166-621c4c0b5fea" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2d6a5a41-e723-5f75-9166-621c4c0b5fea"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2d6a5a41-e723-5f75-9166-621c4c0b5fea" :answer/id #uuid "2d6a5a41-e723-5f75-9166-621c4c0b5fea" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-192" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186124654 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-75a986c0-75fe-5567-a170-fed953f3d35d"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-75a986c0-75fe-5567-a170-fed953f3d35d" :question/id #uuid "75a986c0-75fe-5567-a170-fed953f3d35d" :question/math-academy-id "q-168892" :question/problem "Classify the critical points using the second partial derivatives test.

$0$" :question/worked-solution "The second partial derivative test states that if $a\in {R}^{2}$ is a stationary point of $f(x,y)$ with Hessian determinant $H(a),$ we have the following:

* If $H(a)>0,$ then:

  * if $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}(a)<0,$ then $f$ has a local maximum at $a$ 

  * if $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}(a)>0,$ then $f$ has a local minimum at $a$

* If $H(a)<0,$ then $f$ has a saddle point at $a$

* If $H(a)=0,$ then the second partial derivatives test is inconclusive.

With that in mind, let's classify our critical points:

* $(\pm \sqrt{2},0)$ are local minima of $f$ since $H(\pm \sqrt{2},0)=1\,408>0$ and $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}(\pm \sqrt{3},0)=32>0.$

function is defined for all values of $x$ except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values of $x$ that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-2 & =0 \\ 4x & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{4} \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain is $x\in (-\infty ,\frac{1}{2})\cup (\frac{1}{2},\infty ).$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields "Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y)$ for the following data sets:

$$
x=\{4,\,4,\,-4,\,4\},\,y=\{-1,\,-2,\,7,\,4\}
$$" :question/worked-solution "The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (4+4+(-4)+4) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot ((-1)+(-2)+7+4) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(4-2)(-1-2)+(4-2)(-2-2)+(-4-2)(7-2)+(4-2)(4-2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(2)(-3)+(2)(-4)+(-6)(5)+(2)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[-6-8-30+4] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-40) \\  & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-b3bb762e-f253-556e-b239-591405629ea7"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-b3bb762e-f253-556e-b239-591405629ea7" :answer-field/id #uuid "b3bb762e-f253-556e-b239-591405629ea7" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-dc079189-f549-5385-8ccd-d06d3585f132" :answer-field/choices ["answer-7d8c39eb-cc31-5a79-a9bd-500afe12c950" "answer-dc079189-f549-5385-8ccd-d06d3585f132" "answer-f0431254-6c69-543d-b05b-52b952950087" "answer-7c9e72d7-60a7-512f-af6c-41536483d13a" "answer-fe2cb0ca-1fb3-54af-9579-b241fc473f92"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7d8c39eb-cc31-5a79-a9bd-500afe12c950" :answer/id #uuid "7d8c39eb-cc31-5a79-a9bd-500afe12c950" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-0.5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dc079189-f549-5385-8ccd-d06d3585f132" :answer/id #uuid "dc079189-f549-5385-8ccd-d06d3585f132" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-10" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f0431254-6c69-543d-b05b-52b952950087" :answer/id #uuid "f0431254-6c69-543d-b05b-52b952950087" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7c9e72d7-60a7-512f-af6c-41536483d13a" :answer/id #uuid "7c9e72d7-60a7-512f-af6c-41536483d13a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "10" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fe2cb0ca-1fb3-54af-9579-b241fc473f92" :answer/id #uuid "fe2cb0ca-1fb3-54af-9579-b241fc473f92" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186268978 :question/problem "Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y)$ for the following data sets:

$$" :question/worked-solution "The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-4-3)(2-2)+(2-3)(-9-2)+(6-3)(3-2)+(8-3)(12-2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-7)(0)+(-1)(-11)+(3)(1)+(5)(10)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[0+11+3+50] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 64 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}

"question-5f9a41d3-0af2-58dd-af4a-729df4a947b7" :question/id #uuid "5f9a41d3-0af2-58dd-af4a-729df4a947b7" :question/math-academy-id "q-75321" :question/problem "Let $R=[3,7]\times [0,4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}+7{y}^{2}-10.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the lower Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
L(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?" :question/worked-solution "The lower Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{m}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](images/88/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}+7{y}^{2}-10$ increases as $x$ increases on $[3,7],$ and

- $f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}+7{y}^{2}-10$ increases as $y$ increases on $[0,4].$

![](images/67/67daa328cc6ae4cb37be386c327fb4548844fad2adc10476bdf1147c5a5d4218.png)

As a result, the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion. 

![](images/51/51808df96cf7dd295bfa24aa3641a601c821116e1a0014898ffe705036704a53.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})=2{x}_{i-1}^{2}+7{y}_{j-1}^{2}-10\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the lower Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(2{x}_{i-1}^{2}+7{y}_{j-1}^{2}-10)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $2{x}_{i-1}^{2}+7{y}_{j-1}^{2}-10.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-a1c74bff-65e0-52ab-a110-4fb3d089fed9"] $$

$$

Given that the lower Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
L(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?" :question/worked-solution "The lower Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{m}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](images/88/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that:

- $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x$ increases as $x$ increases on $[0,1]$, and

- $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x$ increases as $y$ increases on $[1,2].$

![](images/67/67daa328cc6ae4cb37be386c327fb4548844fad2adc10476bdf1147c5a5d4218.png)

As a result, the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion. 

![](images/51/51808df96cf7dd295bfa24aa3641a601c821116e1a0014898ffe705036704a53.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})={x}_{i-1}^{2}+{y}_{j-1}^{2}+2{x}_{i-1}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the lower Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}^{2}+{y}_{j-1}^{2}+2{x}_{i-1})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is ${x}_{i-1}^{2}+{y}_{j-1}^{2}+2{x}_{i-1}.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=x+4y+5.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the lower Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by

$$
L(f,P)={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}\boxed{}\,Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}
$$

where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?" :question/worked-solution "The lower Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{m}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion ${R}_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$ over the $x$-axis and ${y}_{i-1}$ and ${y}_{i}$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below. 

![](images/88/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

- $f(x,y)=x+4y+5$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=x+4y+5$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](images/51/51808df96cf7dd295bfa24aa3641a601c821116e1a0014898ffe705036704a53.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i-1},{y}_{j-1})={x}_{i-1}+4{y}_{j-1}+5\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\le i\le m$ and $1\le j\le n.$

Finally, the lower Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}+4{y}_{j-1}+5)Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

"Rewrite $-({x}^{2}-12x+35)$ by completing the square." :question/worked-solution "We begin by completing the square for the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
{x}^{2}-12x+35
$$

First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+35
$$

Then, we *add* and *then subtract* ${6}^{2},$ writing the constant term $35$ last:

$$
{{x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2}}_{⏟}-{6}^{2}+35
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(x-6)^{2}-{6}^{2}+35
$$

Evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(x-6)^{2}-1.
$$

Finally, we substitute this result back into our original expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}-({x}^{2}-12x+35) & =-({(x-6)}^{2}-1) \\  & =-{(x-6)}^{2}+1 \\  & =1-(x-6)^{2}.\end{aligned}

$-{a}^{2}-10a+16$ by completing the square." :question/worked-solution "Notice that the leading coefficient is $-1.$ So, we take out a factor of $-1$ from the entire expression:

$$

$$

Let's now complete the square for the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
{a}^{2}+10a-16
$$

First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{a}^{2}+2\cdot 5a-16
$$

Then, we add and then subtract ${5}^{2},$ writing the constant term $16$ last:

$$
{{a}^{2}+2\cdot 5a+{5}^{2}}_{⏟}-{5}^{2}-16
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(a+5)^{2}-{5}^{2}-16
$$

Evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(a+5)^{2}-41
$$

Finally, we substitute this result back into our original expression:

$$

$$

$$

-1\le t\le 4

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix." :question/worked-solution "Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form. The system corresponding to $M$ is 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+3z=-2 \\ 0x+y-6z=2 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+3z=-2 \\ y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution. 

From the second equation, we get

$$
y-6z=2\,⇒\,y=6z+2
$$

and substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x-2(6z+2)+3z=-2\,⇒\,x=9z+2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=9z+2 \\ y=6z+2 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9z+2 \\ 6z+2 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-199faf22-a58d-5be8-ae85-92e9998ec1eb"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id \{\begin{aligned}x+0y-z=1 \\ 0x+y+3z=2 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-z=1 \\ y+3z=2\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution. 

From the second equation, we get

$$
y+3z=2\,⇒\,y=2-3z
$$

and from the first equation, we obtain

$$
x-z=1\,⇒\,x=1+z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=1+z \\ y=2-3z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+z \\ 2-3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186102776 :answer-field/correct "answer-c453ff5b-68c3-5920-aed9-e4ad1181f6d0" :answer-field/choices ["answer-93a91dfd-17d2-56d8-8eec-c36565a5f78c" "answer-e977f005-547c-5834-a641-8ed9ae0805ff" "answer-360636f3-e809-5ab4-9cc6-cec1e4085529" "answer-c453ff5b-68c3-5920-aed9-e4ad1181f6d0"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-93a91dfd-17d2-56d8-8eec-c36565a5f78c" :answer/id #uuid "93a91dfd-17d2-56d8-8eec-c36565a5f78c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "[\begin{aligned}-1+z \\ 2-3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e977f005-547c-5834-a641-8ed9ae0805ff" :answer/id #uuid "e977f005-547c-5834-a641-8ed9ae0805ff" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "[\begin{aligned}1+z \\ -2-3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-360636f3-e809-5ab4-9cc6-cec1e4085529" :answer/id #uuid "360636f3-e809-5ab4-9cc6-cec1e4085529" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "[\begin{aligned}1+z \\ 2+3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c453ff5b-68c3-5920-aed9-e4ad1181f6d0" :answer/id #uuid "c453ff5b-68c3-5920-aed9-e4ad1181f6d0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "[\begin{aligned}1+z \\ 2-3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-d941de1f-e5bc-5cb7-8728-2a74f1c72d5f" :question/id #uuid "d941de1f-e5bc-5cb7-8728-2a74f1c72d5f" :question/math-academy-id "q-131487" :question/problem "Consider the system

M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 4 & -12 & -20 & -24 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2} & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix." :question/worked-solution "Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 4 & -12 & -20 & -24 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2} & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2} & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-3y-5z=-6 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x-3y-5z=-6
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=-6+3y+5z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-6+3y+5z \\ y=y \\ z=z\end{aligned}
$$

where $y,z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6+3y+5z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-41887196-a674-543e-bbae-cd560d625ecb"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id To solve the system, we can reduce $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as usual. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](images/17/176e4c49ef19bb92d63190dc6674b66ee55b2fdb306293bae65b7f2b2935701d.svg)

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

![](images/a9/a9dd77f0f2ac0f7bd04b5e70fdca3b126d4eb34b0c929caca48c60f138bc644d.svg)

The **basic variables** are the variables of our system whose coefficients are the pivots of the row echelon form matrix. Let's illustrate the pivots of $M\mathbin{:}$

![](images/1b/1b776faa6c69553ce04fbddc4e1aa45e18d7390a32ce34d9e0317b2fa83b8752.svg)

The pivots are

- $m_{11}=1,$ which is the coefficient of $x,$ and

- $m_{22}=1,$ which is the coefficient of $y.$

Therefore, the basic variables are $x$ and $y.$

The remaining variables are called the **free variables**. We have only one free variable in our system, which is $z$.

Finally, we can describe the **general solution** by finding equations for the basic variables in terms of the free variables. In our case, this means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

To do this, we apply the back substitution. From the second equation, we obtain

$$
y - 3z = -5
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	y = -5+3z.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-5+3z)+z=2\,⟹\, & x=-3+2z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is
![](images/e2/e21bb2b83534152d6bf3d1c43efbd301b42717b975f1f9ebaa28ee4bc3ef31bd.svg)
where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as
![](images/de/de7a613bbbde25e555608ebc419106701d47875e238832eab7533bf87b0f1ce8.svg)

Geometrically, this is the vector equation of a line, and any point on the line is a solution to our original system.

If we want to find some **particular solution** of the system, we simply choose some particular value of $z$ and find the corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ on the line. For example, if we choose $z=0,$ then the corresponding values are $x=-3$ and $y=-5$ and the particular solution is $x=-3,$ $y=-5,$ $z=0.$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186129290 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-f7c6f3ba-6533-5a1f-b464-492440ca8f6d"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-f7c6f3ba-6533-5a1f-b464-492440ca8f6d" :question/id #uuid "f7c6f3ba-6533-5a1f-b464-492440ca8f6d" :question/math-academy-id "q-163179" :question/problem "A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 3\}$
and has mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=y,$ where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters.
Given that the center of mass is at $(1,2),$ find the moment of inertia about a line perpendicular to $D$ at a distance of $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\text{m}$ from a parallel line passing through its center of mass." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

First, we find the mass of the plate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =x{|}_{0}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular line through the center of mass $(1,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{M} & ={∬}_{D}((x-\overset{¯}{x})^{2}+(y-\overset{¯}{y})^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}((x-1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}((x-1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2})y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}(x-1)^{2}y+{y}^{3}-4{y}^{2}+4y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}-\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}+2{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{9}{2}(x-1)^{2}+\frac{9}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}(x-1)^{3}+\frac{9}{4}x]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}+\frac{9}{2}-(-\frac{3}{2}+0) \\  & =\frac{15}{2}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a line $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\text{m}$ from the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M \\  & =\frac{15}{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}\cdot 9 \\  & =\frac{15}{2}+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =12\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-bb17ec4b-63ee-5206-af27-3498015a3fd6"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$
\begin{aligned}0+8 & =\frac{(0+2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{6} \\ 8 & =\frac{4}{2}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{6} \\ 8 & =2+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{6} \\ \frac{(y+1)^{2}}{6} & =6 \\ (y+1)^{2} & =36 \\ y+1 & =\pm 6\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the solutions $y=-7,5.$

:question/worked-solution "To find the $x$-intercepts of the paraboloid, we substitute $y=0$ and $z=0$ in the equation of the paraboloid:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-5)^{2}-8(0+2)^{2} & =0+4 \\ (x-5)^{2}-32 & =4 \\ (x-5)^{2} & =36 \\ x-5 & =\pm 6 \\ x & =5\pm 6\end{aligned}

Consider the partition of the rectangular region $R$ shown above and the positive function $f(x,y)$ defined on $R.$ Which of the following gives an expression for the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to this partition.

*Hint: ${M}_{ij}$ denotes the maximum value of $f$ on the subregion ${R}_{ij}$*" :question/worked-solution "To calculate the upper Riemann sum $U$ with respect to the given partition, we compute the sum of the volumes of $3$ rectangular solids, one for each ${R}_{ij}.$

The volume of the rectangular solid corresponding to each subregion ${R}_{ij}$ is given by

$$
{M}_{ij}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{ij}).
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ denotes the maximum value of $f$ on the subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

So in our case, we have

$$
U={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{M}_{13}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{13}).
$$

Notice that

$$
\text{Area}({R}_{11})=\text{Area}({R}_{12})=\text{Area}({R}_{13})=2.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =2\cdot {M}_{11}+2\cdot {M}_{12}+2\cdot {M}_{13} \\  & =2({M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186148895 :answer-field/correct "answer-5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" :answer-field/choices ["answer-5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" "answer-d79c99a8-657e-5f1b-9bf1-7b78ca1c5271" "answer-e0699502-562e-5567-92d0-a0fdd69f0682" "answer-d9dffb21-59c0-5a1f-8919-0d8e4cb108a1" "answer-548eea5d-4b28-5e16-b164-434012c34f08"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" :answer/id #uuid "5a7eda2c-a027-5f95-97f6-e15eace33722" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2({M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13})" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d79c99a8-657e-5f1b-9bf1-7b78ca1c5271" :answer/id #uuid "d79c99a8-657e-5f1b-9bf1-7b78ca1c5271" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}+2{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e0699502-562e-5567-92d0-a0fdd69f0682" :answer/id #uuid "e0699502-562e-5567-92d0-a0fdd69f0682" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d9dffb21-59c0-5a1f-8919-0d8e4cb108a1" :answer/id #uuid "d9dffb21-59c0-5a1f-8919-0d8e4cb108a1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}-{M}_{12}-{M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-548eea5d-4b28-5e16-b164-434012c34f08" :answer/id #uuid "548eea5d-4b28-5e16-b164-434012c34f08" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{M}_{11}\cdot {M}_{12}\cdot {M}_{13}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-b7b6e192-3a06-52fc-8d5f-7a6810288b2c" :question/id #uuid "b7b6e192-3a06-52fc-8d5f-7a6810288b2c" :question/math-academy-id "q-123058" :question/problem "![](images/dd/dd73cb7785de514503cba6a04931a88084172b58826efdf22ea847f256c375fb.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1 & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ (z+1)^{2} & =3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1) \\ (z+1) & =\pm \sqrt{3(\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-1 & \ge 0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}=1$, including its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 1\}.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186323405 :answer-field/correct "answer-8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8a23aa13-d540-5d99-be2b-3b822200ad45" "answer-8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" "answer-6d07251a-4f5b-5fe1-a5c8-5c5e4e7f9bfc" "answer-9bc62f3e-4d97-58eb-bb7f-08bb44e41d57"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8a23aa13-d540-5d99-be2b-3b822200ad45" :answer/id #uuid "8a23aa13-d540-5d99-be2b-3b822200ad45" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}<1\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" :answer/id #uuid "8a7e4314-461a-51dd-8e7e-003b239d4df1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 1\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6d07251a-4f5b-5fe1-a5c8-5c5e4e7f9bfc" :answer/id #uuid "6d07251a-4f5b-5fe1-a5c8-5c5e4e7f9bfc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}<0\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9bc62f3e-4d97-58eb-bb7f-08bb44e41d57" :answer/id #uuid "9bc62f3e-4d97-58eb-bb7f-08bb44e41d57" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\ge 0\}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-1a64d7fd-d80f-53bd-910a-60419647eb47" :question/id #uuid "1a64d7fd-d80f-53bd-910a-60419647eb47" :question/math-academy-id "q-36323" :question/problem "What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the hyperboloid of one sheet $9{x}^{2}+8{y}^{2}-4{z}^{2}=1?$" :question/worked-solution "To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperboloid. 2\. Calculate the value of the function for ${\theta }_{R}.$

3\. Determine whether the resulting value is positive or negative.

![](images/31/312fc3581d9da413254a0eb4dbc64091b286675492821838ba9a65ee06f45a7c.png)

**Step 1**: Since $\theta ={245}^{∘}$ is in the $3$rd quadrant, the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\theta -{180}^{∘} \\  & ={245}^{∘}-{180}^{∘} \\  & ={65}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: The given ratio is $\operatorname{sin}⁡{245}^{∘}$, and therefore we're interested in $\operatorname{sin}⁡{\theta }_{R}=\operatorname{sin}⁡{65}^{∘}.$

**Step 3:** The ratio $\operatorname{sin}⁡{245}^{∘}$ must be *negative* because the sine ratio is *always* negative in the $3$rd quadrant. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{245}^{∘}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡{65}^{∘}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-f5d4c08d-a6b6-51ef-ab36-7ea7637d3cfa"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id :question/id #uuid "3c0d5e56-2169-54d3-9966-1a109d2d5523" :question/math-academy-id "q-105796" :question/problem "Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(0,-1,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,i+3z\,j-2y\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=(6z-1)\,j.
$$" :question/worked-solution "If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & 3z & -2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(3z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)]k \\  & =(-2-3)i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-5\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-5\,i+(6z-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,-1,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(0,-1,1) & =-5\,i+(6(1)-1)\,j \\  & =-5\,i+5\,j.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-743b8050-afb0-5239-be1f-b571663c2f9a"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-743b8050-afb0-5239-be1f-b571663c2f9a" :answer-field/id #uuid "743b8050-afb0-5239-be1f-b571663c2f9a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" :answer-field/choices ["answer-65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" "answer-504fe88b-8989-50fd-9bf6-4fb3a0874f14" "answer-de460cf2-dd72-57b6-89cf-2648f5feed59" "answer-953d0060-629d-5930-8b1a-dc079696c8e2" "answer-cb311272-e389-523f-83ba-df596e274f53"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" :answer/id #uuid "65367f18-ef71-5d52-84f0-4d352c7adcb5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-5\,i+5\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-504fe88b-8989-50fd-9bf6-4fb3a0874f14" :answer/id #uuid "504fe88b-8989-50fd-9bf6-4fb3a0874f14" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-j+k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-de460cf2-dd72-57b6-89cf-2648f5feed59" :answer/id #uuid "de460cf2-dd72-57b6-89cf-2648f5feed59" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-953d0060-629d-5930-8b1a-dc079696c8e2" :answer/id #uuid "953d0060-629d-5930-8b1a-dc079696c8e2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cb311272-e389-523f-83ba-df596e274f53" :answer/id #uuid "cb311272-e389-523f-83ba-df596e274f53" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5\,i-j+5\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186180186 :question/problem "Calculate $∇\times (F+2G)$ at the point $(1,1,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z\,i+{x}^{2}y\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z\,i+(xy-2xyz)\,j-xz\,k.
$$" :question/worked-solution "If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+2G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (2G) \\  & =∇\times F+2∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {x}^{2}z & 0 & {x}^{2}y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}z)]k \\  & =({x}^{2}-0)i-(2xy-{x}^{2})j+(0-0)k \\  & ={x}^{2}\,i+({x}^{2}-2xy)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+2G) & =∇\times F+2∇\times G \\  & ={x}^{2}\,i+({x}^{2}-2xy)\,j+2[{x}^{2}z\,i+(xy-2xyz)\,j-xz\,k] \\  & =({x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}z)\,i+({x}^{2}-2xy+2xy-4xyz)\,j-2xz\,k \\  & ={x}^{2}(1+2z)\,i+({x}^{2}-4xyz)\,j-2xz\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,1,1),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (F+2G))(1,1,1)=3\,i-3\,j-2\,k.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186178660 :answer-field/correct "answer-ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" :answer-field/choices ["answer-0f9b5739-0938-5c65-94b0-f1b4aa69e157" "answer-6a99f0f4-e5ef-5f99-af5c-c942163885d5" "answer-ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" "answer-1067630d-4e4d-554b-9f81-a5561e8e478a" "answer-045f588e-73be-514d-9fd9-46ece75a5e69"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0f9b5739-0938-5c65-94b0-f1b4aa69e157" :answer/id #uuid "0f9b5739-0938-5c65-94b0-f1b4aa69e157" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\,i-3\,j-2\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6a99f0f4-e5ef-5f99-af5c-c942163885d5" :answer/id #uuid "6a99f0f4-e5ef-5f99-af5c-c942163885d5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\,i-\,j+k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" :answer/id #uuid "ebce6acb-ae41-52f5-ac95-a2a586b9f5fb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\,i-3\,j-2\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1067630d-4e4d-554b-9f81-a5561e8e478a" :answer/id #uuid "1067630d-4e4d-554b-9f81-a5561e8e478a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\,i-4\,j-4\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-045f588e-73be-514d-9fd9-46ece75a5e69" :answer/id #uuid "045f588e-73be-514d-9fd9-46ece75a5e69" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5\,i-2\,j+k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-0ea54cb1-a0d4-5539-a164-15702dc537d3" :question/id #uuid "0ea54cb1-a0d4-5539-a164-15702dc537d3" :question/math-academy-id "q-105795" :question/problem "Calculate $∇\times (F-3G)$ at the point $(1,0,9)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=(2\sqrt{z}+x)\,i+xy\,j+{y}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=3{x}^{2}y\,k.
$$" :question/worked-solution "If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-3G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (-3G) \\  & =∇\times F-3∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 2\sqrt{z}+x & xy & {y}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\sqrt{z}+x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{z}+x)]k \\  & =(2y-0)i-(0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}})j+(y-0)k \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-3G) & =∇\times F-3∇\times G \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k-3[3{x}^{2}y\,k] \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k-9{x}^{2}y\,k \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y(1-9{x}^{2})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,0,9),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-3G))(1,0,9) & =2(0)\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{9}}\,j+0(1-9(1)^{2})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-523554aa-2a52-5d37-8cc9-84d837bdff76"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-523554aa-2a52-5d37-8cc9-84d837bdff76" :answer-field/id #uuid "523554aa-2a52-5d37-8cc9-84d837bdff76" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a6aa9a17-9981-5e03-a5c9-1692e6dae401" "answer-8f4111c9-6604-575a-b3bf-8b514228499e" "answer-a4873e67-7fec-50d7-b791-b5ed499f85ae" "answer-3c1f5b71-a8d9-5bee-8b46-73f0baef7978" "answer-1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a6aa9a17-9981-5e03-a5c9-1692e6dae401" :answer/id #uuid "a6aa9a17-9981-5e03-a5c9-1692e6dae401" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-9\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8f4111c9-6604-575a-b3bf-8b514228499e" :answer/id #uuid "8f4111c9-6604-575a-b3bf-8b514228499e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-i-\frac{1}{3}\,k" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a4873e67-7fec-50d7-b791-b5ed499f85ae" :answer/id #uuid "a4873e67-7fec-50d7-b791-b5ed499f85ae" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\,i" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3c1f5b71-a8d9-5bee-8b46-73f0baef7978" :answer/id #uuid "3c1f5b71-a8d9-5bee-8b46-73f0baef7978" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "9\,i-3\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2" :answer/id #uuid "1029c273-1bc6-53a7-8ba2-8c396398f3e2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}\,j" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-1adbaf5f-6695-5acc-8c83-a7d990c62422" :question/id #uuid "1adbaf5f-6695-5acc-8c83-a7d990c62422" :question/math-academy-id "q-105964" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨3z,2x,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xz+y.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,3,2⟩,\,∇f=⟨z,1,x⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,0,0).$" :question/worked-solution "We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ z & 1 & x \\ 3z & 2x & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1(0)-x(2x)]i-[z(0)-x(3z)]j+[z(2x)-1(3z)]k \\  & =-2{x}^{2}\,i+3xz\,j+(2xz-3z)\,k \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(xz+y)⟨0,3,2⟩+⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3(xz+y),2(xz+y)⟩+⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},3(xz+y)+3xz,2(xz+y)+2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},6xz+3y,4xz+2y-3z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,0,0) & =⟨-2(1)^{2},6(1)(0)+3(0),4(1)(0)+2(0)-3(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-358ba299-db97-5c30-b480-8ad69e4c1d58"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-358ba299-db97-5c30-b480-8ad69e4c1d58" :answer-field/id #uuid "358ba299-db97-5c30-b480-8ad69e4c1d58" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" :answer-field/choices ["answer-716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" "answer-9b8592fa-9388-57e4-a3b0-75e82fd0fa0b" "answer-b34859f7-1d1a-5aa1-a406-403532f54aee" "answer-0c8eee1c-f133-5076-90a3-abd6303c7686" "answer-3bc83cd3-ee31-5732-a9e3-7f6452fee0f6"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" :answer/id #uuid "716825f9-f0c6-5e08-968a-88f84d52da1e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨-2,0,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9b8592fa-9388-57e4-a3b0-75e82fd0fa0b" :answer/id #uuid "9b8592fa-9388-57e4-a3b0-75e82fd0fa0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,-2,1⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b34859f7-1d1a-5aa1-a406-403532f54aee" :answer/id #uuid "b34859f7-1d1a-5aa1-a406-403532f54aee" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,0,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0c8eee1c-f133-5076-90a3-abd6303c7686" :answer/id #uuid "0c8eee1c-f133-5076-90a3-abd6303c7686" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨0,3,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3bc83cd3-ee31-5732-a9e3-7f6452fee0f6" :answer/id #uuid "3bc83cd3-ee31-5732-a9e3-7f6452fee0f6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "⟨1,-1,0⟩" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-38f95650-79fd-557c-9c72-45e47bd9ea35" :question/id #uuid "38f95650-79fd-557c-9c72-45e47bd9ea35" :question/math-academy-id "q-131475" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},yz,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{-y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-y,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨{e}^{-y},-x{e}^{-y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,1,2).$" :question/worked-solution "We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {e}^{-y} & -x{e}^{-y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & yz & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(-x{e}^{-y})(0)-(yz)(0)]i-[({e}^{-y})(0)-(x{e}^{y})(0)]j+[({e}^{-y})(yz)-(x{e}^{y})(-x{e}^{-y})]k \\  & =0\,i+0j+(yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2})k \\  & =⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x{e}^{-y})⟨-y,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-xy{e}^{-y},0,-{x}^{2}⟩+⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-xy{e}^{-y},0,yz{e}^{-y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
∇\times (f\,F)(0,1,2)=⟨0,0,\frac{2}{e}⟩.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7200c5c6-834c-582d-bb4f-488640d68497"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$

$$

$$

 

Therefore, the solution is $x>-4.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

inequality $5x-3<2$ on a number line." :question/worked-solution "First, we apply the addition principle, adding $3$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-3 & <2 \\ 5x-3+3 & <2+3 \\ 5x+0 & <5 \\ 5x & <5\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & <5 \\ \frac{5x}{5} & <\frac{5}{5} \\ \frac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} & <\frac{5}{5} \\ x & <1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the solution is $x<1.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

value of $k.$

$k=$

{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{4},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{1}{4}.$ 

From the equation $y=(2x+k)(x-3k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{k}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=3k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{k}{2}+3k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6k-k}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{5k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{4}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5k}{4} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ 5k & =1 \\ k & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-a7afddcb-dc24-5839-bcf0-80fc718004df"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-a7afddcb-dc24-5839-bcf0-80fc718004df" :answer-field/id #uuid "a7afddcb-dc24-5839-bcf0-80fc718004df" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-70b54ca2-ba87-5256-9420-5d2e2bf07f05" :answer-field/choices ["answer-70b54ca2-ba87-5256-9420-5d2e2bf07f05"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-70b54ca2-ba87-5256-9420-5d2e2bf07f05" :answer/id #uuid "70b54ca2-ba87-5256-9420-5d2e2bf07f05" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-213ef30b-cee1-556f-a46a-815fdaa45856" :question/id #uuid "213ef30b-cee1-556f-a46a-815fdaa45856" :question/math-academy-id "q-223693" :question/problem "The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(x-5k)(x+7k)$ is $x=4.$ Find the value of $k.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{5k+(-7k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2k}{2} \\  & =-k\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}-k & =4 \\ k & =-4.\end{aligned}

First, we use the sum rule for differentiation:

$$

$$

Now, we use the constant multiple rule for differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{4})+\frac{∂}{∂x}(8{x}^{2}{y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(8{x}^{2}) & =2\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4})+8{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})-8\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot 4{x}^{3}+8{y}^{2}\cdot 2x-8\cdot 2x \\  & =8{x}^{3}+16x{y}^{2}-16x\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-5406b9c4-8f08-5b5f-8ea0-96705a9a7215"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-5406b9c4-8f08-5b5f-8ea0-96705a9a7215" :answer-field/id #uuid "5406b9c4-8f08-5b5f-8ea0-96705a9a7215" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-9a507ce6-22ce-56f0-ba53-527362e98081" :answer-field/choices ["answer-9a507ce6-22ce-56f0-ba53-527362e98081"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9a507ce6-22ce-56f0-ba53-527362e98081" :answer/id #uuid "9a507ce6-22ce-56f0-ba53-527362e98081" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8x^{3}+16xy^{2}-16x" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198411 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-c7c3402d-fbe9-5875-8d06-b63e54fe220e"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-c7c3402d-fbe9-5875-8d06-b63e54fe220e" :question/id #uuid "c7c3402d-fbe9-5875-8d06-b63e54fe220e" :question/math-academy-id "q-168887" :question/problem "${f}^{′}(x)=$$[\,8{x}^{3}+16x{y}^{2}-16x$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={(∇f)}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Earlier, we found that 

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=8{x}^{3}+16x{y}^{2}-16x.
$$

The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}{y}^{2}-8{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2}-1)=16{x}^{2}y+12y.\end{aligned}

{{field-1}}
